overall.normNotes: Normalizers are the reference CPU's expected quad- and multi-core scores. multi=1000 is modeled from measured per-kernel scaling of a Ryzen 9 9950X3D (8 P-cores with SMT + 4 E-cores) and cross-checked against public all-core ratios (~980-985); provisional until a full-thread i7-12700K result is measured.

profiles.note: Profiles reweight the same measured sub-scores; they never change measurements. 'everyday' equals each component's headline score.

gaming.label: Gaming
gaming.rationale: Most games are limited by a few fast threads, but current engines use 6-8 cores, so all-core throughput still counts.

everyday.label: Everyday
everyday.rationale: Browsing, office work and light content creation: responsiveness plus occasional all-core work.

workstation.label: Workstation
workstation.rationale: Rendering, compiling, encoding and simulation scale across every core.

gaming.label: Gaming
gaming.rationale: Load times are dominated by reads: large assets sequentially, many small files randomly.

everyday.label: Everyday
everyday.rationale: Booting, launching apps and general use: low-queue random reads matter most.

workstation.label: Workstation
workstation.rationale: Large files and parallel I/O: video editing, datasets, VMs and build caches.
